newsitem.title: UAE: Cricket-New Zealand coach says team fitter, stronger.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-New Zealand coach says team fitter, stronger.

text.p: New Zealand's new coach Steve Rixon has promised a stronger and fitter team when they take on World Cup holder Sri Lanka in the opening match of the Singer Champions Trophy one-day tournament on Thursday.

"The spirit of the boys is a lot higher than ever before. There is a marked improvement in fitness levels and, above all, the boys have faith in their abilities," said Rixon on the eve of his first competition with the New Zealand team.

Rixon, who last came to Sharjah as wicketkeeper with the Australian team in 1985, said: "A good depth in batting and a variety in bowling will give the team a fair chance to match the strength of the other two teams in the competition."
Pakistan is the third team in the $30,000 competition.

Rixon said Danny Morrison and Chris Cairns, New Zealand's main strike bowlers, had recovered well from earlier injuries but there was still doubt over the fitness of all-rounder Dipak Patel and medium-pacer Gavin Larsen, who are both nursing calf injuries.
Left-arm spinner Mark Haslam, who injured his hand in the nets, has definitely been ruled out of the first match.
The New Zealanders have not been in action since their unhappy tour of the West Indies in April and May this year when Cairns walked out midway through. But Rixon stressed that that was now history.
"Everything has been resolved and he is eager to perform," he said.
Sri Lanka, still looking for an overseas coach to replace the departing Dav Whatmore, and Pakistan also enter the competition in an upbeat mood.

"Our depth in batting goes to number 10 and the presence of a number of all-rounders is an added advantage," said Duleep Mendis, manager of a Sri Lankan team which is keen to maintain the standards it set when winning the World Cup at the start of the year.
"We have beaten both New Zealand and Pakistan on their home soil in the past so we are not unduly worried."
Pakistan, fresh from a 3-0 one-day whitewash over Zimbabwe in the recent home series, have included five players who will be making their first appearance in Sharjah.
"We are in the process of building a team for the future. But this doesn't mean we are sacrificing on experience. Our team is an ideal blend of young and old," said skipper Wasim Akram.
